name: PasswordPal
summary: A zero-knowledge, local-first desktop password manager built with Tauri v2, React and Rust, where the vault is encrypted on the device before syncing.
whyItMatters: The server only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read. Keys are derived with Argon2id, the vault key is wrapped with AES-256-GCM, and forgotten master passwords can be reset through an Ed25519-signed recovery key.

name: Distributed Auction System
summary: A fault-tolerant real-time online auction built in Go, where four independent nodes coordinate over RPC using classic distributed systems algorithms.
whyItMatters: It implements Bully election, Ricart-Agrawala mutual exclusion, two-phase commit with majority quorum, and Koo-Toueg checkpointing end-to-end, with crash recovery and transaction logging across laptops on Wi-Fi.

name: Talent Radar
summary: A ranking pipeline for a hackathon that picks the top 100 of 100,000 candidates for a Senior AI Engineer job description and writes a CSV with fact-checked reasoning for each finalist.
whyItMatters: It combines FAISS and BM25 retrieval with a Ridge ranker, an availability multiplier and a honeypot filter. The ranking step runs on CPU in under two minutes with no network or LLM-API calls, and every reasoning claim is audited against the candidate's record.

name: Monday.com BI Agent
summary: A conversational assistant that answers founders' questions about sales pipeline and work order data from two Monday.com boards, using Llama 3.3 70B via Groq and the Monday.com MCP server.
whyItMatters: Real board data has messy currencies, dates, nulls and contradictory statuses. A deterministic normalization layer cleans it and every answer discloses data quality issues, including the stage-based fallback used when 75% of deals lack a probability.

name: SentinelFlow
summary: A multi-agent system built for a hackathon that turns meeting transcripts into tracked action items using LangChain, Vertex AI Gemini and AlloyDB, exposed through a FastAPI service.
whyItMatters: An Analyst agent extracts tasks with owners, deadlines and 768-dimension embeddings, and a Watchdog agent audits the database for unassigned tasks so action items are not silently dropped after a meeting.

name: PasswordPal Backend
summary: The Node.js, Express and Supabase API for PasswordPal, handling accounts, device-bound sessions, two-factor auth, account recovery and encrypted vault sync.
whyItMatters: The server never receives the master password or any key that can decrypt a vault. It uses signature-based recovery, per-IP brute-force limits, delta sync with optimistic version locking, and Row Level Security on every table.
